A.subject: Physics
A.text: In a mixed grouping of cells, there are m identical cells in a row and there are n such rows. Each cell is having emf E and internal resistance r. A load resistor R (variable) is connected to this group of cells. Then choose the correct statement out of the following.

Power transfer to load is maximum when current through R is maximum
Maximum power transfer to load is (n²E²R)/(4r²)
A.sol_text:
Equivalent emf of grouping of cells, E_eq. = mE

Equivalent internal resistance, r_eq. = (mr)/n

I = (mE)/(R + (mr)/n) = E/((R/m) + (r/n))

⇒ Current through R will be maximum when R will be minimum
So, power transfer to load is maximum when current in circuit is maximum.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: An object is placed at a distance x (in cm) from a hemisphere of radius R = 24 cm and refractive index μ = 4/3 as shown. When the object is viewed from right side of hemisphere, the image appears at infinity. Value of x is ______.
B.sol_text:
Hint:
n₂/v - n₁/u = (n₂-n₁)/R

Solution:
1ˢᵗ refraction:
μ/v - 1/(-x) = 0 ⇒ v = -μx

2ⁿᵈ refraction:
1/∞ - μ/(-μx+R) = (1-μ)/(-R)
⇒ μ/(μx+R) = (μ-1)/R
⇒ μR = μ²x + μR - μx - R
⇒ x = R/(μ²-μ) = 24/((2/3)×(5/3))
= 54 cm
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.text:
(4) Fibrin

A —(i) Cl₂, Δ—> 
(ii) CN⁻
(iii) H₂O/H⁺

4-Bromophenyl acetic acid.

In the above reaction 'A' is
options: Br attached to benzene ring with CH₂CH₃ substituent
Br attached to benzene ring with CH₃ substituent
Br attached to benzene ring with CH=CH₂ substituent
A.sol_text:
Starting material A is 4-bromotoluene (p-bromotoluene): Br attached to benzene ring with CH₃ substituent.

Step 1: Cl₂, Δ (Chlorination with heat)
The benzylic position is chlorinated: CH₃ → CH₂Cl
Intermediate: 4-Bromo-benzyl chloride (Br-C₆H₄-CH₂Cl)

Step 2: CN⁻ (Cyanide nucleophilic substitution)
The benzylic chlorine is displaced by cyanide: CH₂Cl → CH₂CN
Intermediate: 4-Bromophenylacetonitrile (Br-C₆H₄-CH₂CN)

Step 3: H₂O/H⁺ (Hydrolysis under acidic conditions)
The nitrile is hydrolyzed to a carboxylic acid: CH₂CN → CH₂COOH
Final product: 4-Bromophenylacetic acid (Br-C₆H₄-CH₂COOH)

Therefore, A is 4-bromotoluene, which is option (3): Br attached to benzene ring with CH₃ substituent.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text:
In the cell Pt(s)|H₂(g,1bar)|HCl(aq)|AgCl(s)|Ag(s)|Pt(s) the cell potential is 0.92 V when a 10⁻⁶ molal HCl solution is used. The standard electrode potential of (AgCl|Ag,Cl⁻) is
(Given, (2.303RT)/(F) = 0.06 V at 298 K)
A.sol_text:
Answer : (1)
Solution:
Cell : Pt(s)|H₂(g,1bar)|HCl(aq)|AgCl(s)|Ag(s)|Pt(s)
E_cell = 0.92 V

= E°_{H₂(g),H⁺(aq)} + E°_{AgCl(s)|Ag(s),Cl⁻} - (0.06)/(n) log Q

Cell reaction : (1)/(2) H₂(g) → H⁺(aq) + e⁻

AgCl(s) + e⁻ → Ag(s) + Cl⁻
Net cell reaction:
(1)/(2) H₂(g) + AgCl(s) → Ag(s) + H⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)

∴ Q = ([H⁺][Cl⁻])/(P_{H₂}^(1/2))

10⁻⁶ molal HCl solution is taken
Assuming molality is same as molarity

Q = (10⁻⁶ × 10⁻⁶)/(1) = 10⁻¹²

∴ 0.92 = E°_{AgCl(s)|Ag(s),Cl⁻} - (0.06)/(1) log 10⁻¹²

∴ E°_{AgCl(s)|Ag(s),Cl⁻} = 0.92 + [0.06 × (−12)]
= 0.92 − 0.72
= 0.20 V

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: In the titration of KMnO₄ and oxalic acid in acidic medium, the change in oxidation number of carbon at the end point is ____
B.sol_text:
Answer: 1
Solution:
16H⁺ + 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ → 10CO₂ + 2Mn²⁺ + 8H₂O
During titration of oxalic acid by KMnO₄, oxalic acid converts into CO₂.
∴ Change in oxidation state of carbon = 1
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The resistance of a conductivity cell containing 0.01 M KCl solution at 298 K is 1750 Ω. If the conductivity of the 0.01 M KCl solution at 298 K is 0.152 × 10⁻³ S cm⁻¹, then the cell constant of the conductivity cell is ______ × 10⁻³ cm⁻¹.
B.sol_text:
Answer: 266
Solution:
Molarity of KCl solution = 0.1 M
Resistance = 1750 ohm

Conductivity = 0.152 × 10⁻³ S cm⁻¹

Conductivity = (Cell constant)/(Resistance)

∴ Cell constant = 0.152 × 10⁻³ × 1750
= 266 × 10⁻³ cm⁻¹

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The function f(x) = 2lnx + 5 cot⁻¹x ; x > 0 has
options: Exactly three points of local extremum
Exactly two points of local extremum
Exactly one point of local extremum
A.sol_text:
Given function is
f(x) = 2lnx + 5 cot⁻¹x
f'(x) = 2/x - 5/(1+x²) = (2x² - 5x + 2)/(x(1+x²))

Sign scheme for f'(x) = ((2x-1)(x-2))/(x(1+x²))

       +ve      -        +ve
    0      1/2      2
       point of local    → point of local
       maximum           minimum

when f'(x) = 0, the x = 1/2, 2
⇒ from sign schemes, f(x) has exactly two points of local extremum.

A.text: A man X has 7 friends, 4 of them are ladies and 3 are men. His wife Y also has 7 friends, 3 of them are ladies and 4 are men. Assume X and Y have no common friends. Then the total number of ways in which X and Y together can throw a party inviting 3 ladies and 3 men, so that 3 friends of each of X and Y are in this party, is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (4)
Solution: Answer (4)
Sol. X(4 L 3 G) Y(3 L 4 G)
3 L 0 G 0 L 3 G
2 L 1 G 1 L 2 G
1 L 2 G 2 L 1 G
0 L 3 G 3 L 0 G
Required number of ways
= ^4C_3 · ^3C_3 + (^4C_2 · ^3C_1)^2 + (^4C_1 · ^3C_2)^2 + (^3C_3)^2
= 16 + 324 + 144 + 1
= 485

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The value of p for which the function f(x) = {((4^x - 1)^3)/(sin(p/x)log(1 + x^2/x^2)), x ≠ 0; 12(log 4)^3, x = 0} may be continuous at x = 0, is-
A.sol_text:
For f(x) to be continuous at x = 0, we should have
lim(x→0) f(x) = f(0) = 12(log 4)^3
lim(x→0) f(x) = lim(x→0) ((4^x - 1)^3/x) × ((π/x)/(sin(π/x))) × (px^2/(log(1 + x^2/x^2))) = (log 4)^3 · 1 · p · lim(x→0) (x^2/(x^2/p - 1/12 x^4 + ...))
= 3p(log 4)^3. Hence p = 4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the (m+1)^th, (n+1)^th and (r+1)^th terms of an A.P. are in G.P. and m, n, r are in H.P., then the value of the ratio of the common difference to the first term of the A.P. is
A.sol_text:
Let a be the first term and d be the common difference of the given A.P. Then as given the (m+1)^th, (n+1)^th and (r+1)^th terms are in G.P. ⇒ a+md, a+nd, a+rd are in G.P. ⇒ (a+nd)^2 = (a+md)(a+rd)
⇒ a(2n−m−r) = d(mr−n^2) or d/a = (2n−(m+r))/(mr−n^2) .....(i) Next, m, n, r in H.P. ⇒ n = 2mr/(m+r) .....(ii) From (i) and (ii)
d/a = (2n−(m+r))/(mr−n^2) = 2/n((2n−(m+r)))/((m+r)−2n)) = −2/n

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Consider a triangle whose two sides lie on the x-axis and the line x + y + 1 = 0. If the orthocentre of triangle is (1, 1), then the equation of the circle passing through the vertices of the triangle is
A.sol_text:
As we know mirror image of orthocentre lie on circumcircle.
Image of (1, 1) in x-axis is (1, -1)
Image of (1, 1) in x + y + 1 = 0 is (-2, -2).
∴ The required circle will be passing through both (1, -1) and (-2, -2).
∴ Only x^2 + y^2 + x + 3y = 0 satisfy both.

A.text: Mean and variance for the following data 1, 3, 5, 7, a, 9, 11, b are 5 and 12 respectively, then ab is equal to
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)

Hint:
σ² = Σ(x_i - x̄)² / N

Solution:
x̄ = 5 ⇒ a + b = 4 .....(i)

σ² = Σ(x_i - x̄)² / N = 12

Σ(x_i - x̄)² = 96

16 + 4 + 0 + 4 + (a-5)² + 16 + 36 + (b-5)² = 96 .....(ii)

From (i) and (ii),
a = 1, b = 3
or, a = 3, b = 1

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Consider the line L : x + y = sin⁻¹(2a² − 4a + 3) + cos⁻¹(3a² − 6a + 4) and the circle S : 4x² + 4y² = (sin⁻¹ α)², then which of the following is true about the line and circle?
options: Line passes through the centre of the circle
Line cuts the circle in two distinct point
Line is a tangent to the circle
Line and circle do not intersect
A.sol_text:
2a² − 4a + 3 = 2(a − 1)² + 1 ≥ 1
3a² − 6a + 4 = 3(a − 1)² + 1 ≥ 1
∴ a = 1 is the only value for which line is defined
Hence L : x + y = π/2 & S : 16x² + 16y² = π²
Distance of line from centre of circle > radius of the circle

A.text: The value of ∫_0^(sin²x) sin⁻¹√t dt + ∫_0^(cos²x) cos⁻¹√t dt is
A.sol_text:
We have I = ∫_0^(sin²x) sin⁻¹√t dt + ∫_0^(cos²x) cos⁻¹√t dt

Putting t = sin²u in the first integral and t = cos²v in the second integral, we have
I = ∫_0^x u sin 2u du - ∫_(π/2)^x v sin 2v dv

= ∫_0^(π/2) u sin 2u du + ∫_(π/2)^x u sin 2u du - ∫_(π/2)^x v sin 2v dv

I = ∫_0^(π/2) u sin 2u du = ((-u cos 2u)/2)_0^(π/2) + (1/2)∫_0^(π/2) cos 2u du

= ((-u cos 2u)/2)_0^(π/2) + (1/4)(sin 2u)_0^(π/2) = π/4

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let f be a differentiable function from ℝ to ℝ such that |f(x) - f(y)| ≤ 2|x - y|^(3/2), for all x, y ∈ ℝ. If f(0) = 1 then ∫_0^1 f^2(x)dx equal to
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)
Solution:
Answer (1)
Sol.: f: ℝ → ℝ
and |f(x) - f(y)| ≤ 2·|x - y|^(3/2)
⇒ |(f(x) - f(y))/(x - y)| ≤ 2√(x - y)
⇒ lim(x→y) |(f(x) - f(y))/(x - y)| ≤ lim(x→y) 2√(x - y)
⇒ |f'(x)| = 0
∴ f(x) is a constant function.
∴ f(0) = 1 ⇒ f(x) = 1
∴ ∫_0^1 f^2(x)dx = ∫_0^1 1dx = [x]_0^1 = 1

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The values of x for which the angle between vec(a) = 2x²i + 4xj + k and vec(b) = 7i - 2j + xk is obtuse and the angle between vec(b) and the z-axis is acute and less than π/6, is
options: No such value of x exists
A.sol_text:
The angle between vec(a) and vec(b) is obtuse.

Therefore, vec(a) · vec(b) < 0
⇒ 14x² - 8x + x < 0
or 7x(2x - 1) < 0
or 0 < x < 1/2

The angle between vec(b) and the z-axis is acute and less then π/6. Therefore,

(vec(b) · vec(k))/(|vec(b)||vec(k)|) > cos π/6 (∵ 0 < θ < π/6 ⇒ cos θ > cos π/6)

⇒ x/√(x² + 53) > √3/2

or 4x² > 3x² + 159
or x² > 159
⇒ x > √159 or x < -√159 (ii)

Clearly, (i) and (ii) cannot hold together

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: The number of relations, on the set {1, 2, 3} containing (1, 2) and (2, 3), which are reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, is _______.
B.sol_text:
Answer : 4
Solution:
(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3) ∈ R

Since (1, 2), (2, 3) ∈ R, (1, 3) must ∈ R
Possible cases :
Case-1 : All of (2, 1), (3, 2), (3, 1) ∉ R → 1 relation.
Case-2 : Only one of (2, 1), (3, 2), (3, 1) ∈ R → 3 relations.
Note that exactly two of (2, 1), (3, 2), (3, 1) ∈ R is not possible because if two of these ∈ R, third must ∈ R to make the relation transitive.
Total number of relations = 4
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.
